subject: Insurance
title: The 1906 San Francisco Earthquake
description: A micro-lesson that makes The 1906 San Francisco Earthquake usable.

hook.text: After the 1906 San Francisco earthquake, homeowners set their own houses on fire.

buildup.text: Insurance companies covered fire but excluded earthquakes. Desperate homeowners committed arson to collect.

discovery.text: The fires caused more damage than the earthquake itself. Insurance incentives turned a disaster into an inferno.

twist.text: Some insurers went bankrupt anyway. Lloyd's of London paid every claim in full, cementing its global reputation.

climax.text: 1906 proved that insurance design shapes behavior in catastrophes. Wrong incentives create worse outcomes.

punchline.text: Earthquake excluded, fire covered. Homeowners chose arson.

quiz.question: Why did homeowners set fires after the 1906 earthquake?
options: Fire insurance paid but earthquake insurance didn't
